correctness.rationale: On the diagonal, t'=4t−3(1+2a)t². Scaling by u=3(1+2a)t/4 gives logistic-four, which is a factor of doubling by u=sin²(πθ); its arcsine probability is ergodic. Differentiating gives the fixed line and zero-sum plane multipliers 4(1−2u) and 4(1−ku), k=(2+a)/(1+2a), so logarithmic ergodic averages suffice. Their isolated interior or endpoint zeros are integrable, and their finite-time preimages are null. Under u=(1−cos θ)/2 the transverse log integral is log 4 plus the cosine-log average with A=1−k/2 and B=k/2. Applying Jensen to the quadratic z²+(2A/B)z+1 on the circle gives log k for k≥1 and 2 log(1+√(1−k)) for k<1; the radial k=2 case gives log 2. The identities k−1=(1−a)/(1+2a) and 1−k=(a−1)/(1+2a) on the respective sides yield the two constants. At a=1, F(x)=(4−3s)x maps the closed tetrahedron to itself and preserves composition before any hit of zero. Its derivative is (4−3s)I−3x 1ᵀ, with an invariant radial line span(p) and zero-sum plane along each fixed-composition orbit, giving the printed ray spectrum. The product change of variables x=(4u/3)p has volume Jacobian proportional to u²; arcsine and Lebesgue are equivalent in u. Ergodicity for a countable dense set of continuous tests then gives weak empirical convergence for volume-almost every point. The mean vector of each limit is (2/3)p; any specified empirical limit thus has at most one ray of typical initial conditions, a volume-null set. These are analytic checks of RESULT.md, not execution of verify.py or a claim about basins outside the tetrahedron.
